translations.answer: Issue #255 and merge PR #256 change the negative epsilon in the old certificate criterion to positive epsilon, using a separate `OSQP_DIVISION_TOL` to determine if the certificate vector is non-zero; the documentation is aligned with the final paper. This change was officially integrated into `develop-0.x`. Due to later #485 reporting a positive epsilon in the singleton feasible region, this experience only confirms the historical merge with the original MRE, and does not prove that the criterion covers all degenerate boundary cases.
translations.applicability: Directly corresponds to the 2020 `develop-0.x` fix; subsequent versions and singleton feasible cases must be validated together with #485.
translations.credibility.rationale: The issue has been closed, the environment is clear and there is no conflict. There is formal documentation or precise reference to an independent reproducibility.
translations.details.attempts.0: PR #256 replaces the primal/dual conditions with a positive epsilon and uses `OSQP_DIVISION_TOL` to handle zero norm; the documentation is synchronized.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: The code, final paper Section 3.4, and current certificate inequality are compared; the degenerate and singleton feasible region regression sets are preserved.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: The historical upgrade to `develop-0.x` containing the merge commit `fad7cf2` fixes the old non-detection; this does not prove that all degenerate boundaries are correct.
translations.details.environments.0: 2020 `develop-0.x` branch; Issue provides a scalar MRE from CVXPY, PR provides a direct OSQP Python MRE.
translations.details.limits.0: PR did not include a dedicated test file in the visible diff; #485 later reported a positive epsilon in the singleton feasible region, so this issue must retain the conflict.
translations.details.outcomes.0: PR was approved and merged; the author/maintainer provided a minimal example that failed before the fix.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why might the old OSQP not detect a simple infeasible QP? What was merged into `develop-0.x`?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: After upgrading the solver, test explicitly infeasible, ordinary feasible, and singleton/deg feasible QP cases.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The maintainer confirmed that the old code had a negativity test written as a negative epsilon, and used `eps_*_inf` to itself determine the certificate vector non-zero.
translations.details.symptoms.0: For any `eps_prim_inf`, an infeasible scalar problem can be constructed with an interval equal to that epsilon, making the old condition unable to produce a certificate.
translations.source.title: The old OSQP infeasibility certificate fix has been merged but later raised boundary concerns.
translations.terms.1: Primal infeasibility tolerance (原始不可行容差)
translations.title: What fix was merged into the project when it failed to identify problems like `x ≤ 0, x ≥ 1e-4`?
